fields.description_1: DCA Dienstverlening had to help organisations identify the right cleaning or specialist-recovery service and move toward a quotation. The live website covers office and hotel cleaning, floor care, façade work, industrial cleaning, construction handover, drone cleaning and inspections, so the offer is broad. Visitors need a clear way to understand which service fits the location, what the company can handle and how to request help without reading every page first. The project therefore needed strong service grouping, trust information and visible next steps. Mobile users also needed the same hierarchy when comparing services or opening the quotation route. The portfolio text had to stay factual and simple, using the current service offer without inventing operational or conversion results that were not independently verified.
fields.description_2: For DCA Dienstverlening, I structured the WordPress experience around cleaning categories, specialist services, proof, practical information and quotation actions. The homepage gives the broad offer first, then separates regular cleaning, specialist cleaning and newer drone services so organisations can move toward the relevant route. Reviews, client logos and working-method content support trust without replacing the service explanation. Clear quotation and contact actions stay close to the sections where a visitor is likely to decide. The same hierarchy is preserved on mobile, with service choices and calls to action kept easy to scan. This gives DCA Dienstverlening a portfolio story that reflects the real website and current service range, while avoiding unsupported claims about customer satisfaction, lead growth or other outcomes beyond what the public site itself documents.

fields.description_1: ACF Image Auto Filler had to reduce repetitive image assignment without making unsafe assumptions about complex ACF structures. Editors may need to map many Media Library images to normal ACF Image fields or featured images, but bulk writes can overwrite existing values or target the wrong content if the mapping is unclear. Nested repeaters, flexible content, galleries and clone fields add even more ambiguity, so the plugin deliberately does not auto-fill those structures. The workflow needed preview mapping, optional overwrite confirmation, manual mapping, batch limits, rollback and an audit trail. The portfolio text also had to explain that the plugin does not send content to external services. The central challenge was controlled bulk editing: make repetitive image work faster while keeping supported field types, permissions and recovery options explicit.
fields.description_2: I built ACF Image Auto Filler as a WordPress admin workflow that starts with selected content, supported fields and Media Library images, then shows the mapping before any write. Top-level ACF Image fields are supported, along with direct Image fields inside Groups when enabled, and featured images can be handled separately. Existing values are skipped unless overwrite is explicitly enabled. Manual mapping, batch mode and CSV dry-run export give administrators more control when automatic order is not enough. Each saved run can keep rollback data for the current user, while a small admin audit log records the operation. Capability and per-item permission checks protect bulk actions. The plugin intentionally excludes repeaters, flexible content, galleries and clones from automatic filling, keeping the solution bounded instead of guessing how complex nested ACF data should be written.

fields.description_1: Wehear4u had to help visitors understand a humanitarian hearing-care mission and see how they could contribute. The organisation supports children and adults with hearing problems, including work in Kenya, and promotes donations of used hearing aids, financial support and partnerships. That creates several audiences with different next steps: someone may want to understand the mission, donate equipment, support a trip, become a collection point or share the initiative. The website therefore needed to connect the human story with practical participation without turning every section into a donation request. Mobile visitors also needed a clear route through mission information and actions. The portfolio text had to remain respectful, factual and easy to understand, avoiding invented impact numbers or medical claims beyond the organisation's publicly described work and goals.
fields.description_2: For Wehear4u, I structured the WordPress presentation around the mission, the people the initiative aims to support and the practical ways visitors can help. Story and purpose come first, followed by clearer routes for donating hearing aids, contributing financially, becoming a partner or learning about the work in Kenya. Calls to action are placed where they connect naturally to the surrounding content rather than competing on every section. The same priorities stay visible on mobile so the page remains readable even when emotional storytelling and practical information appear together. The project story therefore shows how the website supports awareness and participation without overstating measured outcomes. It keeps the organisation's hearing-care focus understandable to donors, partners and general visitors while leaving medical impact claims to the organisation and its qualified partners.

fields.description_1: Fidelyaa had to explain a consultancy offer that spans strategic advice, guidance, reintegration and activation programmes, tenders, analysis and implementation support. Government organisations and SMEs may arrive with very different problems, so a single generic consultancy message would not explain where each service fits. The website needed to separate the main routes while still showing that they belong to one advisory approach. Visitors also needed enough context to understand whether they were looking for strategy, programme support or implementation before starting a conversation. The case study therefore had to describe the actual consultancy work in plain English rather than rely on broad words such as expertise or solutions. Mobile structure and contact routes needed the same clarity, and the portfolio text had to avoid outcomes that were not measured or publicly supported.
fields.description_2: For Fidelyaa, I structured the WordPress presentation around the main advisory and programme areas, with separate context for strategy, guidance, reintegration, activation, tenders, analysis and implementation support. This helps government organisations and SMEs move from a specific organisational question toward the part of the offer that is most relevant. Service explanations stay concise, while supporting context shows how advice and execution relate without collapsing them into one generic proposition. Contact routes remain visible after the relevant information so a conversation follows naturally from the service being considered. I used direct headings and simple English to keep the portfolio case understandable to non-specialists. The solution describes the real information architecture and consultancy scope without adding unsupported claims about client outcomes, programme effectiveness or business growth that were not verified through the available project sources.

fields.description_1: SooCool for WooCommerce had to connect ecommerce orders with an external transport platform without creating duplicate fulfilment work or unsafe order-state changes. Shipping integrations handle customer and delivery data, remote API calls, labels, delivery moments and status updates, so failures can affect both operations and WooCommerce records. Retries must not blindly create a second transport order, and webhook messages must not be trusted without verification. The plugin also needed HPOS-compatible order access, background processing and explicit boundaries around checkout behaviour. The portfolio text therefore had to explain the engineering problem rather than present the integration as a simple API connection. The key challenge was keeping WooCommerce and the logistics provider synchronized while protecting credentials, personal data, replay-sensitive webhooks and ambiguous remote states from causing uncontrolled fulfilment changes.
fields.description_2: I built SooCool for WooCommerce around controlled order submission, delivery scheduling, status handling, retries and shipping-label workflows. Order access uses WooCommerce APIs so the integration remains compatible with HPOS rather than relying on legacy post storage. Remote submissions can run asynchronously, and existing transport orders are linked instead of recreated blindly. Webhooks use timestamped HMAC verification and replay protection before they can influence local state. Ambiguous remote statuses do not overwrite WooCommerce orders automatically, while retries and maintenance recovery handle temporary failures more safely. API credentials are masked in the interface and logs avoid intentionally storing complete sensitive payloads. Delivery-moment selection is validated server-side. The portfolio solution shows the real integration boundaries and failure handling, without claiming that external logistics becomes error-free or that every checkout implementation has proven feature parity.

fields.description_1: Content Sync Manager had to make large WordPress content and media updates reviewable before they become bulk writes. Pages, posts, WooCommerce products, custom post types, ACF fields and media information can be spread across many editing screens, making coordinated changes slow and difficult to inspect. Import workflows add risk because an incorrect file can overwrite structured content, rename media or touch builder-related references. The project therefore needed preview binding, validation, permission checks, backups and explicit confirmation around higher-risk operations. Media filename changes also required a usage scan so fixed URLs or inaccessible pages could block a dangerous rename. The portfolio text needed to show this safety model instead of describing the plugin as generic automation. The central problem was efficient bulk editing without turning convenience into uncontrolled changes across a WordPress installation.
fields.description_2: I built Content Sync Manager as an admin-only workflow for controlled export, review, import and recovery of WordPress content and media. It supports pages, posts, WooCommerce products and supported custom content while dynamically detecting relevant ACF fields. Imports are prepared and validated before writes, then tied to the reviewed source so a different file cannot silently replace the approved preview. Backups and recovery paths support rollback when changes need to be reversed. Media workflows include usage context, ACF paths and guarded filename changes; renaming fails closed when builder metadata, unsupported storage or incomplete edit permissions make references unsafe to update. Higher-risk actions require capability checks and explicit confirmation. The solution lets teams work with larger structured updates while preserving a clear boundary between reviewing proposed changes and actually modifying live WordPress content.

fields.description_1: The WooCommerce Egaline Calculator had to turn project measurements into a product quantity customers could actually order. Flooring or material purchases may depend on area, layer thickness, kilograms per square metre, bag weight and product variation, so a normal quantity field does not explain how much material is required. The calculation also needed to stay connected to live pricing, discounts, tax handling and the cart instead of producing an isolated estimate that disappears at checkout. Invalid numerical inputs or inconsistent dependencies could create confusing quantities. The portfolio text therefore needed to explain the customer-facing calculation problem, not describe an abstract internal tool. The main challenge was linking technical material rules with a simple WooCommerce buying flow that preserves calculated information through product selection, cart and order processing.
fields.description_2: I built the Egaline Calculator directly into the WooCommerce product journey before the add-to-cart action. Customers can enter project measurements such as area and thickness, while the plugin calculates the required material quantity and updates related values in real time. Product-specific settings define bag weight, material density, calculation mode and optional discount thresholds. The calculator supports simple and variable products, keeps relevant calculation data with the cart item and preserves that information in the order. Input validation prevents invalid numerical values from becoming purchase quantities, while WooCommerce remains responsible for normal tax and pricing behaviour around the calculated amount. The responsive interface keeps the controls usable on smaller screens. The portfolio solution shows how domain-specific measurement rules were connected to an actual ecommerce transaction instead of leaving the calculation separate from purchasing.

fields.description_1: Exam Registration Manager had to make examination sign-up clearer than handling dates, candidate details and registration status through disconnected forms or manual administration. An exam workflow combines scheduled sessions, available places, participant information and confirmation steps, so the interface must show what can be selected and what information is required before submission. Administrative users also need a structured way to review registrations without turning ordinary content screens into an improvised booking database. The project therefore needed a focused WordPress workflow with clear boundaries between public registration and back-office management. The portfolio text had to describe that workflow in simple English without inventing pass rates, registration growth or other results that were not measured. The main problem was practical coordination: connect exam dates and participant registration in one manageable process while keeping form behaviour and administrative review understandable.
fields.description_2: I structured Exam Registration Manager around a dedicated WordPress registration flow for exam sessions and participant information. The public side guides candidates from an available exam option to the fields needed for a complete registration, keeping the next action visible rather than mixing it with unrelated site content. Administrative views organise submitted registrations so staff can review the relevant session and participant details from one workflow. Validation is applied before information is accepted, and the data model keeps exam-related records separate from normal page content. The interface uses clear labels and compact steps so the process remains understandable on desktop and mobile. The portfolio solution focuses on the real management problem the plugin addresses: making exam scheduling and registration easier to coordinate inside WordPress, without claiming educational outcomes or operational improvements that were not verified through project evidence.

fields.description_1: Services Overview Manager had to solve a content-architecture problem that appears when business services are maintained as scattered page sections or manual lists. As the offer grows, categories, summaries, prices and related details can become inconsistent, while visitors have no single place to search or filter what is available. The plugin therefore needed a dedicated service content model that editors could maintain independently from the presentation. Import and export also had to stay controlled because CSV changes can affect many service records at once. The public interface needed lightweight search and category filtering without loading unnecessary assets across the whole site. The portfolio text had to explain this structured-content problem rather than present the project as a generic service page. The key challenge was maintaining one reliable service source while keeping the frontend overview flexible and easy to browse.
fields.description_2: I built Services Overview Manager around a dedicated WordPress service post type, categories and structured metadata. Editors can maintain services in one content model instead of updating repeated manual lists across different pages. A reusable shortcode renders the public overview with search and category filtering, giving visitors a clearer way to narrow the offer. Controlled CSV import and export support larger administrative updates, while nonces, capability checks, sanitization and upload validation protect those actions. Frontend and admin assets are scoped to the places where they are needed, and uninstall behaviour remains conservative so content is not removed casually. The solution separates service data from layout while still giving the public site a searchable presentation. The portfolio case explains the actual architecture and management workflow without claiming traffic, lead or conversion improvements that were not independently measured.

fields.description_1: Sparx Entertainment Agency had to help people planning weddings, birthdays or corporate events explore a broad entertainment catalogue without losing the route to an enquiry. The offer includes DJs, live musicians, bands, special acts and event extras, so visitors may start with an event type rather than a specific performer. A flat list would make very different options difficult to compare and would separate inspiration from booking intent. The website therefore needed clear entertainment categories, enough context to understand each direction and visible contact routes near the relevant choices. Mobile browsing also mattered because image-heavy entertainment content can become cumbersome on small screens. The portfolio text had to describe the actual event and entertainment offer in simple English, avoiding invented booking figures or claims about audience response that were not measured through the project sources.
fields.description_2: For Sparx Entertainment Agency, I structured the WordPress experience around entertainment types and event needs. Visitors can move from broad choices such as DJs or live music into more specific artists, bands, special acts and supporting extras without returning to a generic overview each time. Visual content provides inspiration, while short descriptions explain what each category represents and enquiry actions remain close to the options being considered. The page hierarchy keeps the entertainment catalogue central rather than burying it beneath agency marketing text. Responsive layouts preserve the same discovery route on smaller screens, where images, category cards and contact actions need especially clear priority. The portfolio solution therefore shows how a broad creative offer was turned into an understandable booking-oriented structure, without adding unsupported claims about event enquiries, conversion rates or commercial performance.
